tonal.role: optional reproducible composition, integration, provenance and distribution of independently versioned development tools and targets

project.name: Tonal
project.architecture: generic exact-commit composition of independent development tools, targets and optional support components

composition_model.rule: An example is not part of a Tonal composition until an exact repository, version and immutable commit are explicitly added to the manifest and lock.

tlaloc.authority: behavioral development, bounded Tlaloque swarm experiments, prompt-first distillation, failure-to-regression conversion and target-specific development laboratories

origami.authority: Origami representation semantics, semantic/native navigation, state machines, visual grammar, ROSETTA, Writer/Reader contracts and Origami releases

ownership.component_semantics: owned only by each component/target repository
ownership.development_artifact_authority: development tool until accepted by target

notes: Tlaloc and Origami remain independently usable and authoritative for their own contracts.
Tonal can compose Tlaloc, Blueprint Framework or other development systems once exact pins are supplied; unpinned examples are never treated as installed components.
A Tonal verification proves the declared composition is reproducible and its configured checks pass. It does not promote Origami semantics, visual profiles or model capabilities.
A Tonal composition references exact commits, never floating branches.

The current composition includes the failure-driven Native semantic regression tooling in Tlaloc alpha.15 and the matching semantic-first T2 correction in Origami alpha.12; this composition does not claim held-out VLM success.

The experimental-spine branch repins Tlaloc alpha.21 to exact commit dd5b167bfcea61b638bf042624d5dbbc25bc0d1f so TONAL runtime prototypes can consume the complete public tlaloc.local/behaviorlab/prototypelab projection API. This is an experimental composition pin, not a new Tlaloc release or a promotion claim.

TONAL T1 introduced a runtime subsystem under runtime/ (module tonal.local/runtime) that consumes qualified Tlaloques via tlaloc.local/behaviorlab/tlaloquekit. On this experimental branch, runtime/experience additionally adapts native TONAL RunRecords into Prototype Lab Episodes while keeping RunRecord as execution authority and requiring explicit experiment evaluation instead of treating execution completion as semantic correctness.
